title: Synthetic fleet hunt: one unsigned binary with a Run-key autorun beside a client-approved remote-support agent

provenance.method: Fictional Amcache, Autoruns and Prefetch rows from a proactive hunt, written for this corpus and graded as the importers and tagger grade them; the approved labels stand in for a client baseline.

seedEvents.description: Amcache: execution from a user-writable path - C:\Users\Public\Libraries\svcupd.exe (unsigned, no publisher) @ HUNT-WS-17
Autoruns: HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run - Entry=SvcUpd - Image=C:\Users\Public\Libraries\svcupd.exe - enabled, not verified @ HUNT-WS-17

findings.confidenceReason: One unsigned program in a user-writable folder with its own Run-key autorun, seen on one host only; nothing shows what it does.
findings.title: Rare unsigned svcupd.exe with a Run-key autorun on HUNT-WS-17
findings.description: svcupd.exe ran from C:\Users\Public\Libraries on HUNT-WS-17 with no publisher, and an enabled, unverified HKCU Run entry starts it at logon. It is the one anomaly in this hunt; its purpose is not established.

cannedOutput.summary: Proactive hunt: one anomaly ranked — an unsigned svcupd.exe with a Run-key autorun on HUNT-WS-17. ScreenConnect on HUNT-WS-02, HUNT-WS-05 and HUNT-WS-11 is approved by the client and runs as expected. Coverage is unknown, so no absence is claimed for hosts not shown.

nextSteps.action: Collect svcupd.exe from HUNT-WS-17 and check its hash and signature
nextSteps.rationale: The binary decides whether this is unapproved software or a real compromise.

uncertainties.basis: Only its execution and its autorun entry are recorded.
uncertainties.gap: The binary has not been collected or analysed.

uncertainties.basis: No hunt coverage record is available.
uncertainties.gap: Which hosts answered the hunt is not known.

forbiddenConclusions.claim: The client-approved ScreenConnect agent running on the fleet hosts is evidence of attacker remote access.
The rare binary is part of an attack chain with lateral movement, ransomware or a named threat actor behind it.
